To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the quality of a system can be measured in terms of the quality of the system's activities and that the quality of these activities is independent of the properties of the system itself.
maintainability is a function of the number of changes to the system and that the maintainability of a system is proportional to its flexibility and inversely proportional to its complexity.
maintainability is a quality property of a software system that can be defined as the ability to make a change in the system without introducing new errors.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following topics: 1. A new quality modelling approach that allows the definition of maintainability and flexibility in a way that is understandable to software developers and managers. 2. A set of maintainability criteria that is based on this modelling approach and is applicable in practice.
the development of a maintainability measurement approach for object-oriented software systems.
the following questions: How can maintainability be measured? What is a maintainable system? How can maintainability of systems be controlled?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the quality of the software is not good enough.
maintainability is the ability to maintain a system without causing an unacceptable degradation of its properties.
maintainability can be defined as the ability to change a system at low cost and risk.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are able to define a set of maintainability criteria and their relationships to each other and the software product.
maintainability is the ability of a software system to be changed in a controlled way to meet new requirements.

we have developed a maintainability model that allows to effectively measure the maintainability of a software system and that we have shown how to use this model to drive maintainability improvement.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the maintainability of software systems can be effectively defined and measured by means of a quality model.
maintainability and flexibility are not a property of the code but rather a property of the system.
the quality model is not a mere academic exercise but a powerful instrument that can be used to effectively drive software quality improvement in large scale commercial organizations.
